title: Polymer analyticity and dilute continuum correlations

items.title: Abstract polymer model and connected coefficients

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 5, Cluster Expansion
references.locator: §§5.2–5.3, PDF pp. 2–5 (printed pp. 220–223): finite polymer model, compatible subsets, connected graph coefficients, and the formal expansion.

references.title: Daniel Ueltschi, Cluster expansions and correlation functions
references.locator: §2, PDF pp. 1–4: measure-space partition function, connected graph coefficient, and the cluster expansion.

items.statement:
An abstract polymer model consists of an at most countable set $\Gamma$ (finite or in bijection with $\mathbb N$), a reflexive symmetric relation $\sim$ on $\Gamma$ (so $\gamma\sim\gamma$ and $\gamma\sim\eta$ implies $\eta\sim\gamma$), and an activity function $z:\Gamma\to\mathbb C$. Its elements are called polymers, and $\gamma\sim\eta$ means that the two polymers are incompatible. A subset $X\subseteq\Gamma$ is compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. For real and natural summands, finite-index sums and products are enumeration-independent. For complex summands, define a finite sum or product by any enumeration and repeated addition or multiplication in $\mathbb C$; associativity and commutativity make the result independent of the enumeration. The empty sum is $0$ and the empty product is $1$. For each finite $V\subseteq\Gamma$, define the finite-volume partition polynomial

$$Z_V(z):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\\X\text{ compatible}}}\ \prod_{\gamma\in X}z_\gamma,$$

where the empty subset contributes $1$.

Write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $\binom{[n]}2:=\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in[n],\ i\ne j\}$. A simple graph on $[n]$ is a pair $([n],E)$ with $E\subseteq\binom{[n]}2$; a path is a finite vertex list with distinct vertices and each consecutive pair an edge. A graph is connected when every two vertices are joined by a path. A cycle is a vertex list $(v_0,\ldots,v_k)$ with $k\geq3$, $v_k=v_0$, $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$ distinct, and each consecutive pair an edge; a tree is a connected simple graph with no cycle. For $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq1$, let $\mathcal C_n$ be the set of connected simple graphs on $[n]$ and let $\mathcal T_n$ be the set of trees on $[n]$. The set $[n]$ is finite; its power set is finite, so its subset $\binom{[n]}2$ is finite; the power set of that edge set is finite as well. Each simple graph on $[n]$ is determined by an edge set in this last power set, so $\mathcal C_n$ and $\mathcal T_n$ are finite.

For an ordered tuple $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\in\Gamma^n$, put $f_{ij}:=-\mathbf 1_{\{\gamma_i\sim\gamma_j\}}$ and define the connected coefficient

$$U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_{ij}.$$

For $n=1$, $\mathcal C_1$ contains the one-vertex graph and the empty edge product equals $1$. These are finite polynomial and coefficient definitions; they assert no convergence.

items.title: Rooted connected polymer sums obey the tree majorant

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 5, Cluster Expansion
references.locator: §5.4, Theorem 5.4 and its complete proof, PDF pp. 5–8 (printed pp. 224–227): the Kotecký–Preiss rooted connected-cluster majorant.

references.title: Daniel Ueltschi, Cluster expansions and correlation functions
references.locator: §2, Theorem 1 and complete rooted-cluster induction, PDF pp. 1–4.

items.statement:
Let $(\Gamma,\sim,z)$ be an abstract polymer model, and let $a:\Gamma\to[0,\infty)$. Interpret each countable sum over polymer labels of nonnegative terms as the supremum of its finite subsums in $[0,+\infty]$, and interpret a nonnegative series as the supremum of its increasing partial sums in $[0,+\infty]$. Suppose

$$\sum_{\eta\sim\gamma}|z_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma).$$

For each fixed root $\gamma\in\Gamma$, define the nonnegative rooted connected-cluster sum

$$R_\gamma:=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(n-1)!}\sum_{\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n\in\Gamma}|U_n(\gamma,\gamma_2,\ldots,\gamma_n)|\prod_{j=2}^n|z_{\gamma_j}|$$

Then $R_\gamma$ is well-defined as a possibly extended nonnegative series and satisfies $R_\gamma\leq e^{a_\gamma}$.

items.title: A strict polymer majorant gives a zero-free finite partition function

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 5, Cluster Expansion

items.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an at most countable set (finite or in bijection with $\mathbb N$) and let $\sim$ be a reflexive symmetric relation on $\Gamma$ ($\gamma\sim\gamma$ and $\gamma\sim\eta$ implies $\eta\sim\gamma$). Let $V\subseteq\Gamma$ be finite, and fix maps $w:V\to\mathbb C$ and $a:V\to[0,\infty)$ and a radius $r>0$. Call $X\subseteq V$ compatible when no two distinct elements of $X$ are related by $\sim$. Suppose there is $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ such that

$$\sum_{\substack{\eta\in V\\\eta\sim\gamma}}r|w_\eta|e^{a_\eta}\leq(1-\varepsilon)a_\gamma\qquad(\gamma\in V).$$

For $t\in\mathbb C$, define $Z_V(t):=\sum_{\substack{X\subseteq V\\\text{and }X\text{ is compatible}}}\prod_{\gamma\in X}(tw_\gamma)$. Define the connected series

$$L_V(t):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{t^n}{n!}\sum_{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\in V}U_n(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n)\prod_{i=1}^nw_{\gamma_i}.$$

Then $L_V$ converges absolutely and uniformly on every closed subdisc strictly inside $|t|<r$, may be differentiated there term by term, and satisfies $Z_V(t)=\exp(L_V(t))$ for $|t|<r$. Thus $Z_V$ has no zero in this disc. Here an analytic logarithm of $Z_V$ on the disc means a holomorphic function $L$ with $\exp(L(t))=Z_V(t)$ there; the logarithm $L_V$ is normalized by $L_V(0)=0$.

items.title: Stable continuum Mayer coefficients obey an integrated tree bound

references.title: Suren Poghosyan and Daniel Ueltschi, Abstract cluster expansion with applications to statistical mechanical systems
references.locator: §6, Proposition 6.1(a), Lemmas 6.2–6.3 and complete proof, PDF pp. 11–14; §3, classical gas assumptions and convergence criterion, PDF pp. 4–5.

references.title: Aldo Procacci and Sergio A. Yuhjtman, Convergence of Mayer and Virial expansions and the Penrose tree-graph identity
references.locator: §2.1, Proposition 1 and the stable-potential bound, PDF pp. 5–6; §§3.1–3.3, the partition scheme, Penrose identity and proof of Proposition 1, PDF pp. 6–10.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq2$ and write $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A simple graph on $[n]$ is $([n],E)$ with $E$ a set of unordered two-element subsets of $[n]$; a path is a finite vertex list with distinct vertices and consecutive pairs in $E$; connected means every two vertices are joined by a path; a cycle is a vertex list $(v_0,\ldots,v_k)$ with $k\geq3$, $v_k=v_0$, $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$ distinct, and consecutive pairs in $E$; a tree is a connected graph with no cycle; a forest is a graph with no cycle. Finite sums and products over graph, edge, vertex, and subset sets below are enumeration-independent; the empty sum is $0$ and the empty product is $1$. Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, let $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be an even Borel pair potential with no $-\infty$ values, and suppose it is stable with constant $B\in\mathbb R$, $B\geq0$. Fix $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$, set $e^{-c(+\infty)}:=0$ for every $c>0$, define the Mayer function $f_\beta(x):=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and suppose

$$C_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty.$$

Let $\mathcal C_n$ be the connected simple graphs on $[n]$ and let $\mathcal T_n$ be the trees on $[n]$. These families are finite because $[n]$ has finitely many unordered two-element subsets and each graph is determined by a subset of those edges. A spanning tree of a finite graph is a tree with the same vertex set and a subset of its edges. A leaf is a vertex incident to exactly one edge. Put

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j).$$

For every configuration $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in(\mathbb R^d)^n$,

$$|U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)|\leq e^{2\beta Bn}\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_n}\ \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(T)}|f_\beta(x_i-x_j)|,$$

where $\mathcal T_n$ is the set of labelled trees on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. In particular,

$$\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}|U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)|\,dx_2\cdots dx_n\leq e^{2\beta Bn}n^{n-2}C_\beta^{\,n-1}.$$

items.title: The stable continuum Mayer pressure series converges in an explicit dilute disk

references.title: Suren Poghosyan and Daniel Ueltschi, Abstract cluster expansion with applications to statistical mechanical systems
references.locator: §3, classical gas and explicit convergence condition, PDF pp. 4–5; §6, Proposition 6.1(a), PDF pp. 11–14; §7, Theorem 2.1 proof, PDF pp. 15–17.

references.title: Aldo Procacci and Sergio A. Yuhjtman, Convergence of Mayer and Virial expansions and the Penrose tree-graph identity
references.locator: §2.1, Theorem 0 and Proposition 1, PDF pp. 3–6; §3 tree-graph identity and proof of Proposition 1; §4 Mayer coefficient integration and pressure-series bound, PDF pp. 11–12.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure. All indices $n,N$ below range over $\mathbb N$. Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, an even Borel pair potential $v:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ with no $-\infty$ values, stable with constant $B\in\mathbb R$, $B\geq0$, and inverse parameter $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$. Put $e^{-c(+\infty)}=0$ for every $c>0$, $f_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta v(x)}-1$, and $C_\beta=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|f_\beta(x)|\,dx<\infty$. For each $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n\geq2$, use

$$U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\sum_{G\in\mathcal C_n}\prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}f_\beta(x_i-x_j),$$

where $\mathcal C_n$ is the set of connected simple graphs on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$; set $U_1=1$. For $L\in\mathbb R$ with $L>0$, let $\Lambda_L=[-L,L]^d$ and write $|\Lambda_L|:=\lambda_d(\Lambda_L)=(2L)^d$; define

$$\Xi_L(z):=\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^N}{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}\exp\!\left(-\beta\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}v(x_i-x_j)\right)\,dx_1\cdots dx_N,$$

with the $N=0$ term equal to $1$. Set $b_1(L)=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n(L):=\frac1{n!|\Lambda_L|}\int_{\Lambda_L^n}U_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_1\cdots dx_n.$$

Also set $b_1=1$ and, for $n\geq2$,

$$b_n:=\frac1{n!}\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^{n-1}}U_n(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\,dx_2\cdots dx_n.$$

Let $\mathcal D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|e^{2\beta B+1}C_\beta<1\}$ when $C_\beta>0$, and let $\mathcal D=\mathbb C$ when $C_\beta=0$. On $\mathcal D$, the finite-volume connected pressure series $p_L(z):=\sum_{n\geq1}b_n(L)z^n$ and the limiting Mayer pressure series $p(z):=\sum_{n\geq1}b_nz^n$ converge absolutely and locally uniformly, are differentiable term by term, and satisfy

$$\Xi_L(z)=\exp\!\bigl(|\Lambda_L|p_L(z)\bigr),\qquad \lim_{L\to\infty}p_L(z)=p(z).$$

The convergence and derivative limits are uniform on every compact subdisc of $\mathcal D$. The pressure limit here is along centered cubes only.

items.title: Hard-core spheres in the explicit dilute domain

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction, Chapter 5, Cluster Expansion
references.locator: §5.6, the hard-core interaction and polymer convergence example, PDF pp. 9–11 (printed pp. 228–230).

references.title: Suren Poghosyan and Daniel Ueltschi, Abstract cluster expansion with applications to statistical mechanical systems
references.locator: §3, classical gas with stable interactions and explicit sufficient low-fugacity condition, PDF pp. 4–5.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\in\mathbb N$ with $d\geq1$, a hard-core diameter $a\in\mathbb R$ with $a>0$, and $\beta\in\mathbb R$ with $\beta>0$. For $x=(x_j)_{j<d}\in\mathbb R^d$, write $\|x\|_2:=\sqrt{\sum_{j<d}x_j^2}$, and let $B(0,a):=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2<a\}$. Let $\lambda_d$ denote Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^d$. Define the hard-core pair potential $v_a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ by $v_a(x)=+\infty$ when $\|x\|_2<a$ and $v_a(x)=0$ when $\|x\|_2\geq a$. Its stability constant may be chosen as $B=0$, the function $x\mapsto e^{-\beta v_a(x)}-1$ is $-1$ on $B(0,a)$ and $0$ elsewhere, and its absolute integral is $C_\beta=\lambda_d(B(0,a))$. For a complex activity $z\in\mathbb C$, with modulus $|z|$ as defined by $|x+iy|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$, the sufficient analytic domain is $e|z|\lambda_d(B(0,a))<1$.
